evidence.section: 3.2. Experimental tensile and deformation behaviors at room temperature
evidence.quote: Comparing the quasi-static tensile microstructure of heat-treated (see Fig. 5 a) and cold-drawn wire (see Fig. 4 a) reveals that the twin lamella in the heat-treated wire is significantly wider than that of cold-drawn wire. These wider twins may originate from the widening of inherited mature twins during heat treatment. Besides, abundant newly tiny twins are present in the heat-treated wire.

A high strain rate leads to more thinner twins, which hinders dislocation more effectively and hence results in higher strength.

The enhanced mechanical property mainly results from the increasing twinning by increasing strain rate or/and decreasing temperature. In particular, coupled high strain rate and cryogenic temperature lead to abundant nanoscale twins and secondary twins, further increasing ductility and strength.
